# `KPEX/2.5D` Engine   {#sec-engine-kpex-2_5D}

This analytical extraction engine is separate from the **PEX25D interchange format** described in @sec-pex25d. `kpex extract --2.5D` selects the engine; `kpex pex25d` generates a geometry and material description without running an engine.

Field solvers are precise, yet slow, they are useful to obtain a golden reference.

For most use cases, a faster engine is desirable.
`KPEX/MAGIC` is such an engine, but the `MAGIC` code is tightly coupled with the database, layer/via design choices, and user interface of `MAGIC`. For example, it runs single-threaded.

Therefore, the `KPEX` 2.5D Engine intends to implement the concepts and formulas of `MAGIC` (see @sec-magic-cap-types), but in a way that is best suited to the `KLayout` API, and is modular and open for parallel execution.

![`KPEX` 2.5D Engine](figures/kpex-engine-2.5D-overview.svg){#fig-kpex-engine-2.5D-overview}

In @fig-kpex-engine-2.5D-overview, we see that as in the `KPEX/FasterCap` engine (see @sec-kpex-fastercap), a "LVS" script is used to extract the connectivity information and create an LVS report database.

As mentioned in @sec-into-klayout-pex-prototype-status, `KPEX` uses the KLayout API.
During the course of this project, in cooperation with Matthias Köfferlein, the `KLayout` API was extended, in order to simplify parasitic extraction.

The engine uses those new API classes to extract parasitic capacitances:

- `klayout.db.PolygonNeighborhoodVisitor` (since `0.30.1`): used during the extraction of overlap capacitances (see @sec-magic-cap-types-overlap-capacitance)
- `klayout.db.EdgeNeighborhoodVisitor` (since `0.30.1`): used during the extraction of sidewall capacitances (see @sec-magic-cap-types-sidewall-capacitance) and fringe capacitances  (see @sec-magic-cap-types-fringe-capacitance)
- Geometry classes with properties in `klayout.db` (since `0.30.1`): store net information directly on polygons, edges, edge pairs and boxes

The engine uses those new API classes to extract parasitic resistances:

- `klayout.pex` module (since KLayout `0.30.2`)
   - `klayout.pex.RNetExtractor`: used to extract resistance networks
   - `klayout.pex.RExtractorTech`: minimal process stack description for conductor and via layers


## Choosing the Level of Detail {#sec-2_5d-modes}

`--mode CC` keeps each connected net equipotential. `--mode R` breaks its conductors into a resistance network. `--mode RC` places extracted capacitances on that distributed network as well, so the position of a load along a wire affects the simulated response.

Grounded capacitance is an explicit approximation: `--mode C` uses ideal conductors, while `--mode RC --coupling grounded` retains distributed resistance. The development-version options, floating-conductor treatment and standalone postprocessing are described in @sec-capacitance-coupling.

The capacitance model has separate area-overlap, facing-sidewall and fringe terms. Polygon integration preserves their geometric meaning for sloped boundaries (@sec-polygon-capacitance). It does not turn the analytical model into a field solver or remove the need to check its coefficients against the intended technology.

The halo limits which neighboring geometry participates in sidewall and fringe extraction. Keep the same halo and fringe normalization when comparing runs. Recent neighborhood batching and rectangular-shield interval subtraction reduce repeated geometric work while retaining the polygon path for general shapes. They do not justify shrinking the halo to obtain a faster result.
